newsitem.title: JAPAN: IBJ says to cut long-term prime to 2.7% for July.
newsitem.headline: IBJ says to cut long-term prime to 2.7% for July.

text.p: The Industrial Bank of Japan (IBJ) said on Tuesday it was cutting its long-term prime rate by 0.2 percentage point to 2.7 percent for July, effective from Thursday.
The IBJ also said it would set the coupon rate of its debenture to be issued this month at 1.8 percent, down from two percent in June.
The prime rate, which is applied to loans of one year and longer to Japanese long-term credit banks' most creditworthy clients, is reviewed every month, reflecting market trends.

The IBJ customarily sets its long-term prime rate, at which long-term credit banks charge their most creditworthy customers for loans of over one year, 0.9 percentage point above its debenture coupon rate. Bank debentures are the long-term credit bank's major fund-raising tool.
IBJ's June two percent five-year bond debentures were traded at 1.8 percent on Tuesday after being traded at 1.79 percent and 1.8 percent on Monday, bond traders said.

The other two long-term credit banks, the Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan Ltd and Nippon Credit Bank Ltd, are scheduled to announce their new long-term prime rates and terms for July debentures on Wednesday.
